Benzimidazoles
The benzimidazole family of fungicides includes carbendazim, benomyl, thiabendazole and fuberidazole. Although imazalil and
thiophanate-methyl are also included in this fungicide class, they lack the typical benzimidazole moiety consisting of a fusion of
benzene and imidazole ring system (Fig. 9). These compounds inhibit microtubule formation by binding to free b-tubulin mono-
mers. Thiabendazole is a slightly toxic compound also used to treat some helminthiases in veterinary medicine and in humans.
Carbendazim is the main metabolite of benomyl and thiophanate-methyl, and produces toxic effects on the seminiferous epithe-
lium by inhibiting polymerization of b-tubulin, thus interfering with microtubule formation. Carbendazim also exerts androgenic
effects which are not related to the androgen receptor but to a lower expression of estrogen receptors (ERa and b). Carbendazim
speciﬁcally acts on the blood-testicular barrier, affecting germ cell migration (Durand et al., 2017; Pisani et al., 2016).
